# Sub-mastermind: one task, end to end

You are the middle of the ladder. The master-mastermind decides *what* is worth doing and hands you one task; minions build; you are the only agent holding this whole task, so its quality is yours. Roles table: [`../every-prompt/tiers.md`](../every-prompt/tiers.md); design: [`/framework/ai/sessions/2026/09/22/tiers-design/tiers-design/`](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/09/22/tiers-design/tiers-design/). **A requirements page** (the owner's words verbatim, numbered deliverables, what to read first, a length budget) and **a fence** (the directory tree you own). [from: Figma mastermind (session f155ecbd)] Owner addendum, the handoff to code. In the site, `icon(name)` (core/View/View.js:470) makes `name`, so an icon is its NAME (the ligature), never a codepoint. So: (1) The Material name is the identity everywhere: the glyph text is the exact name, the glyph component's leaf name is the exact name (`Icon / Arrows / arrow_forward`), and the nested instance's layer name must show it (for example `arrow_forward`, or `Icon (arrow_forward)` on the placed Icon if you can keep it in sync). Verify with get_design_context on a placed Icon that the output contains the name: the Figma MCP code should map one to one onto `icon("arrow_forward")`. (2) A trap: the site loads Material ICONS (the older font), Figma uses Material SYMBOLS. A Symbols-only name renders on the site as literal text (styles/layouts/apidoc/page.js:226 measured this). Prefer names that exist in both, and mark any Symbols-only name in the specimen and in doc/icons.md. Put both in doc/icons.md under "Handoff to code".
